dev_notes: src/commands/audit.mjs and src/git.mjs, the only place the package shells out to git. residue() walks the commits since the last audit (git.commitFiles) and keeps a product file only when none of its owners was recorded in the same commit or moved in the open release, plus files no entry owns that still exist, plus globs that match nothing (deadGlobs). The brief carries per-group diffs (80 lines each, 1,200 in all). The stamp goes through `ledger audit complete`, never a hand-edit: it verifies the commit is an ancestor of HEAD, and the brief always carries an explicit --commit. Every audit is kept in .ledger/audits.json with its mode. `audit confirm <id>` still works, accepting that entry's open why questions. No git, or a shallow clone, degrades to a full sweep with no gate.

history.name: The ledger audit
history.description: The command ledger audit finds capabilities that shipped without the ledger recording them, such as work done without a coding agent that read the project's instructions. It prints a brief for a coding agent: the range since the last audit, the changed paths grouped into batches, and the commit subjects behind them. An audit covers everything since the last one, or the whole codebase with --full, which is the only way to find a capability the baseline survey missed. The agent records what it finds and then stamps the commit it audited, so the tool knows how much of the repository has not been examined yet. A release with unaudited work behind it cannot be cut, and the refusal says how many commits and files are outstanding. A project that started with ledger bootstrap is already stamped, because the baseline survey counts as a full sweep.

history.reason: Its job is part of ledger prepare now, which reads the code since the last edition for work nobody recorded in the same session that writes the edition, instead of a separate step with a stamp the cut waited for.

events.what: It looks only at code the ledger hasn't accounted for, and hands the agent the diffs, instead of every changed path and the commit subjects.
events.why: Every commit counted, so the gate fired after work that had been recorded properly, and an agent handed only file names had to work out again which entry each file belonged to.

events.what: The ledger audit is no longer part of the product.
events.why: Its job is part of ledger prepare now, which reads the code since the last edition for work nobody recorded in the same session that writes the edition, instead of a separate step with a stamp the cut waited for.
